# Statistics theory

What the model is doing, in enough detail to defend it in review, and no more.

::: {.callout-warning}
Draft. Structure fixed, prose in progress.
:::

## The problem: correlated estimates within a study

Why estimates sharing one reference group cannot be treated as independent, and
what goes wrong when they are.

## Reconstructing the within-study covariance

The Greenland and Longnecker result [@greenland1992], and the refinements by
study design [@orsini2006].

## Two-stage estimation

Fit a trend in each study, then pool the trends. The practical reference is
@orsini2012.

## One-stage estimation

A single linear mixed model across all studies, which keeps studies that
two-stage drops [@crippa2019].

## Choosing a functional form

Linear, quadratic, restricted cubic splines. Where to put knots and why the
default is defensible but not sacred.

## Heterogeneity in a dose-response model

What heterogeneity means when the thing varying is a curve rather than a number.

## Alternatives worth knowing

Robust error meta-regression [@xu2018], Bayesian formulations [@hamza2021], and
when each is the better answer.
